spatial_claims.claim: Produce AB beyond B and mark C on the produced part so that BC = b (collinear point placement on a line extension)

configuration_map: All geometric objects are collinear: AB is a line segment, C is placed on the extension of AB beyond B with BC = b, forming segment AC = AB + BC. No triangles, circles, angles, or non-trivial spatial relationships exist. The proof reasons entirely about commensurability (in length and in square), proportions, and definitional criteria for rational, binomial, and first binomial straight lines.
skip_reason: The proof is purely algebraic/proportional, dealing with commensurability relations, fourth proportionals, and the definitions of binomial and first binomial lines. The only geometric action is a trivial collinear construction (extending a segment and marking a point), which has no configuration complexity and cannot produce spatial contradictions. Book 10 commensurability theory, not spatial geometry.
